previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, and peripheral vascular disease, was admitted with shortness of breath due to acute on chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and pulmonary edema. He developed acute kidney injury likely from cardiorenal syndrome and was found to have concomitant pneumonia, which was treated with antibiotics. He became anuric and was managed in the ICU with aggressive diuresis, including a furosemide drip, which restored urine output and improved renal function. His mental status declined temporarily due to metabolic encephalopathy, but resolved without acute neurological injury. His INR was subtherapeutic, requiring heparin bridging before warfarin stabilization. A CO2 angiogram showed no renal artery stenosis. By discharge, he was breathing comfortably, his labs had normalized, and he was transitioned to oral torsemide 100 mg daily, increased carvedilol, and adjusted insulin. He was discharged home with services, with follow-up planned and instructions to monitor weight and symptoms.
